clue.text: Church without members is low on appeal

parts.note: members here are limbs, so lacking them is being armless

explanation.surface: A church congregation has dwindled away and the place has lost its draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests a congregation, but it means limbs: arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no charm has little attraction, so it is lacking in appeal.

clue.text: Male with pen, artist that's a cold-blooded sort

parts.note: a pen is a female swan and its mate is the cob
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An artist and a man holding a pen together make a heartless type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a reptile, an animal that is literally cold-blooded.

clue.text: Coming from a Republican, how s/he sees a Democrat?

parts.note: taken as written
a Republican regards a Democrat as an opponent, a rival

explanation.surface: A question about how a Republican views a member of the other American party.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of turning up, which as a noun is a coming.

clue.text: Reportedly produced a low morose feeling

indicators.note: reportedly marks words that only sound like the answer

parts.note: a cow lows, i.e. moos

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have made a gloomy sound out of sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like 'downcast' but is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mood means a sulky bad temper, a gloomy spell of feeling.

clue.text: Lamb starter taken from celebrity chef

indicators.note: the first letter, the starter, is taken off the chef's name

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook

explanation.surface: A TV chef removes a lamb dish from her menu of starters.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote as Elia; Delia Smith is a well-known British TV cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb, so it refers to that writer.

clue.text: Paper probes drunkard with problem, which is yielding material

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the paper sits inside the drunkard

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
FT is the Financial Times
an issue is a difficulty

explanation.surface: A newspaper investigates a drunk's troubles, which proves rewarding material.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft tissue is the body's non-bony parts such as muscle and fat, which give under pressure.

clue.text: Large city is withdrawing source of power

indicators.note: withdrawing means going back, so the city and the word is are read backwards

parts.note: the Great Wen was Cobbett's nickname for London, so a wen is a large city
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big city's power station is being taken offline.
explanation.walkthrough: WEN is a crossword favourite for a big city, from 'the Great Wen', an old nickname for London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is tendon, and figuratively strength or the means of force, so a source of power.

clue.text: Fight with police and a large old copper, perhaps

parts.note: a scrap is a scuffle
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tussle with officers and a big veteran policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded copper is a typical example of waste metal collected for recycling.

clue.text: Gets to be more ascetic? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase stops short of its final letter

parts.note: an ascetic would need less

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is turning more self-denying.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate them, and 'it gets me' means it annoys me.

clue.text: Sets pawns out in area dominated by queen

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chess player lays out pawns on part of the board the queen controls.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is a decoy: the queen is the insect colony's queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp colony is ruled by its egg-laying queen, so her nest is her domain.

clue.text: Pub fight getting heated, we hear, in seaside town

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is only to sound like the letters entered

parts.note: something being heated is put in a furnace

explanation.surface: A brawl in a pub turns nasty in some coastal resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a town on the Cumbrian coast of north-west England; 'in Furness' sounds like 'in furnace'.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a real port town on the coast of Cumbria, so it is an example of a seaside town.

clue.text: Rule adopted by a very old Aussie PM

indicators.note: being adopted by something means being taken into it, so the rule letter goes inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly Australian prime minister takes on a new regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is not a prime minister but post meridiem; ARVO is Australian slang for afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang the afternoon is the arvo, and PM marks the hours after noon.

clue.text: Something painter does in society: hits the bottle!

parts.note: to tipple is to drink alcohol habitually

explanation.surface: An artist goes out in high society and drinks heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is the technique of applying paint or ink in small dots, a thing an artist does.

clue.text: Tad confused about excluding women in accommodation

indicators.note: about means going around the other piece
confused letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the three letters of this word are the ones jumbled
with women excluded you have just men

explanation.surface: A slightly muddled boy is barred from women's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation' looks like lodging but means adapting.
explanation.definitionFit: Accommodation can mean an adaptation or compromise, a change made to fit.

clue.text: Good learner naturally has admitted driving's done here

indicators.note: admitting something lets it in, so the learner letter goes inside

parts.note: of course means naturally, obviously

explanation.surface: A capable learner driver naturally owns up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' looks like the motoring of a learner but is the long tee shot in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a long golf shot from the tee, so it is played on the links.

clue.text: Sporty or Scary Spice — awful or nice to listen to?

parts.note: both Sporty Spice (Mel C) and Scary Spice (Mel B) of the Spice Girls are named Mel
odious means hateful or horrible

explanation.surface: A question of whether a Spice Girl's singing is dreadful or lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; two members, Sporty and Scary, share the first name Mel.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodious describes tuneful, pleasant sound, so something agreeable for the ears.

clue.text: Roughly grasp piece by composer on the radio

parts.note: a chessman is a piece

indicators.note: on the radio means heard, so the composer's name is used for its sound

parts.note: Handel, the German-born British baroque composer

explanation.surface: A work by a composer is broadcast on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle is to move or treat someone roughly by force.

clue.text: Result of case of extradition ending with appeal

indicators.note: ending with tells us the appeal piece comes last
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the word whose outer letters, its first and last, are kept
to sue is to petition or make an appeal

explanation.surface: An extradition case is concluded by an appeal being lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to ensue is to follow on as a consequence, so to result.

clue.text: Labour henchman holds back prime minister

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read from right to left
the phrase holds the answer inside its run of letters

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of Labour and the start of henchman holds the name

explanation.surface: A Labour Party heavy restrains the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nehru led India's government from independence in 1947 until 1964.

clue.text: One's embraced by Sarah friskily — this is spicy stuff

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside
friskily suggests playful movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the five letters of the name are the ones mixed up
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: Someone gets a frisky hug from Sarah, which is hot stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste, a fiery condiment.

clue.text: Advocate of social hierarchy in battle with big stars

parts.note: a feud is a long-running fight
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A believer in class divides is fighting famous celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism ranks lords over vassals and serfs, so a supporter of it backs a rigid class order.

clue.text: Bury shrouds for one, two or three?

indicators.note: the burial word wraps around the next piece like a shroud

parts.note: to inter is to bury
eg (for example) is what 'for one' means

explanation.surface: A burial of an example; a question about counting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town but is a verb. 'one' does double duty, reading on into the list of examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Two and three are whole numbers, each an example of an integer; the question mark flags the examples.

clue.text: Making bubbly adult limit energy at first

indicators.note: at first places the energy letter ahead of the limit word

parts.note: to ration is to limit supply

explanation.surface: An instruction to cap a grown-up's energy, or else a fizzy drink being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne but here means fizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerating a liquid charges it with gas, the process that makes it fizzy.

clue.text: Mix porridge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to blend by stirring
second meaning: British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is the oat breakfast you stir, but in British slang 'doing porridge' means serving time in jail, and 'stir' is prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means blend with a spoon, and the noun is slang for jail or jail time.

clue.text: Recital of Frost's poetry

indicators.note: a recital is spoken, so the frost word is used for its sound

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A reading aloud of the poems of Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet but is ice crystals, rime.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme can mean verse in general, as in 'nursery rhyme' or 'in rhyme'.

clue.text: What may make models flipping love haircare product

indicators.note: flipping turns the pieces over so they are read upwards in this down light

parts.note: gel is a styling product for hair

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about a hair product used by fashion models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' suggest fashion; they are toy constructions, and 'flipping' poses as a mild swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego bricks are a construction toy used to build small replicas, so it can make models.

clue.text: Forceful flick, using the other hand

indicators.note: the other hand swaps left for right, so the L becomes R

parts.note: a flick is a film

explanation.surface: A strong flick made by swapping to the other hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means resolute and strong, as in a firm push or firm handling.

clue.text: Peter is thus made peer in a demoralising way

definitions.meaning: removing the heart, the central T, from the name turns it into the word peer
the plain sense: in a manner that saps courage

explanation.surface: A man called Peter gets ennobled, yet somehow the process is depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as DIS-HEARTENING-LY: take the heart (middle letter T) out of PETER and you get PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that saps morale or hope is done discouragingly, which is the plain adverb.

clue.text: Perfect law that's been revoked

parts.note: ex means former, describing a thing no longer in force
an act is a statute

explanation.surface: A repealed statute is described as flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise or accurate, without error, as perfect can mean as a verb or adjective.

clue.text: Turn up without car on eastern sector of Amazon?

indicators.note: on joins the eastern letter to the rest, placing it ahead
without in its old sense of outside, so the arrival word goes around the car

parts.note: to come is to arrive or turn up
a Merc is a Mercedes

explanation.surface: Someone arrives without a vehicle in the eastern part of the Amazon region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' looks like the rainforest but is the online retailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Online trading is the business of the retailer Amazon, the question mark flagging it as an example.
